summary: Instagram is where almost all your audience is: most Hindi videos get 400-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly stay under 100 views. The best videos are short 'X doesn't do what you think, it actually does Y' explainers about a single sensor or gadget (clap switch, gyro robot, mic, IR robot). Videos that were only posted on YouTube, plus the English Arduino video, got almost nothing, and the newest videos (soil sensor, UV, geyser) are getting the fewest views so far.
winningPattern: A single familiar sensor or gadget, usually robot or clap-switch themed, with a myth-busting Hindi hook of the form 'X doesn't do [obvious thing], it only does [surprising thing]' or a bold 'without this, the robot falls' claim. Titles are short, mix Hinglish with one emoji, and end with #shorts. Instagram Reels is the main platform: shares come from relatable curiosity ('Why sunburn on cloudy days?'), saves from robot and maker explainers, and likes from quick visual demos.
doMore: Post every video on Instagram Reels as well as YouTube; videos left off Instagram got zero reach there.
Make more robot and clap-switch style explainers with a dramatic demo in the first second, since these get the most views and saves.
Use the 'doesn't do X, only does Y' hook, but pair it with an everyday situation (sunburn, dustbin, tap) that people want to share.
Add a save-worthy ending like a one-line wiring tip or pin list, since saves signal maker value.
Make a short series (e.g. 'Robot Senses Part 1, 2, 3') so viewers come back for the next one.
stopDoing: Stop posting only to YouTube or only in English; the Hindi Instagram audience is the one responding.
Stop dry question titles like 'X Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' with no surprise; they get almost no views.
Stop repeating near-duplicate topics (many clap switch, IR and tap videos) so closely together.
